interpreter.name: Claude
interpreter.context: fresh session, no prior knowledge; analysis from contact sheet and facts only

object.short_description: Rectangular stepped pyramid built from light grey studded bricks, with a narrow one-stud-wide column rising from the centre and a small minifigure-like figure with a grey helmet and tan tunic standing on top.
object.construction_material: plastic building bricks (appearance only; material not verifiable)

estimated_real_size.basis: Footprint about 0.096 m wide in file units; the detected stud pitch is about 5.5 % of that width (about 5.2 mm). If the studs are a standard 8 mm brick pitch, the base would be about 0.146 m wide and the whole model about 0.19 m tall. The model may be scaled in the file, so this is an estimate.

structure.overall_shape: stepped taper (rectangular stepped pyramid) with a slender central column and a small figure on the very top

components.name: stepped pyramid body
components.description: Rectangular footprint (about 0.096 x 0.075 in file units) with about seven receding levels. Light flat tiles or plates form the ledges and grey studded bricks fill in between.

components.name: central column
components.description: Narrow, roughly one-stud-wide light shaft rising from the top step to the figure; it appears to be about as tall as the upper half of the pyramid.

components.name: figure on top
components.description: Small minifigure-like character with a grey helmet that has a small knob or spike on top. It wears a tan or brown upper garment with blue and white details and dark brown lower parts. One arm is visible, extended to the side in the right and left views.

components.name: base plate row
components.description: Flat light base course around the lowest level, made of tiles or plates with visible seams.

repeated_elements.what: round studs on the exposed step surfaces and the top view

defects: 380 connected components, consistent with separate bricks
thin diagonal triangulation lines on flat faces are visible, probably a rendering or tessellation artefact
figure is textured while the bricks are almost uniformly light grey

evidence.statement: All four side views show a symmetric stepped taper with about seven receding levels, each with studs on the exposed ledges.
The top view shows a regular grid of round studs on a rectangular footprint, with the figure at the centre.
A narrow column rises from the centre of the top step and carries a small humanoid figure with a helmet and a tan tunic.
Facts report 380 connected components, 22 geometries, 0 degenerate faces and a non-watertight mesh, consistent with an assembly of separate bricks.
Facts report footprint type 'stepped_taper' with 7 plateaus and a periodic stud pattern with pitch about 5.5 % of extent a.
98.9 % of the surface is near-white or light grey (#edede9). The few colours (tan, blue, brown) belong to the figure.
Mirror symmetry about both horizontal axes is rated high; mirror symmetry about the vertical axis is low, as expected for a tapering shape.
The figure is small compared with the pyramid, about 10 % of the total height, and its scale matches a minifigure on studs of about the same width as its body.

hypotheses.label: Brick-built stepped pyramid with a central pillar and a figure on top, a toy or display model
Monument or column on a stepped base with a statue of a warrior or soldier on top

candidate.label: commemorative column with statue on stepped plinth

hypotheses.label: Model of a specific real monument, for example a victory or memorial column
Free design without a specific real-world model
Minifigure display stand or podium, with the stepped pyramid only as a pedestal

questions_for_owner: Is the model based on a real monument or building, and if so which one?
Is it an official kit, a MOC (own creation) or a digital assembly, and in which software was it made?
What do the figure and the helmet represent, for example a character, a soldier or a ruler?
Which scale applies, in particular the real size of the studs in the file units?
notes: Hypotheses overlap and need not sum to 1. The scale estimate assumes standard 8 mm stud pitch and is uncertain. The side views show about seven steps, which agrees with the 7 plateaus in the facts.
